title: Evaluation of the Effect of the Guide Socket on the Primary Stability of the Miniscrew in a Polyurethane Cortical Bone Model
content: There are only a few studies in the literature that have evaluated the effect of pilot drilling to create a guide socket on the primary stability of miniscrews. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of creating a guide socket during miniscrew insertion on the primary stability of the miniscrew in an in vitro PU cortical bone model. Polyurethane blocks with a density of 60 pcf were used for in vitro cortical bone modelling. 1.8 x 0.0 mm self-drilling mushroom-head titanium miniscrews were used. A 1 mm diameter surgical fissure drill was used to create the guide sockets in the study groups. A total of 45 miniscrews were included in the study in the no guide, 2mm deep guide and 4mm deep guide groups. The insertion torque values for the miniscrews in the 4mm guide socket group were significantly lower than the other groups, and the removal torque values for the miniscrews in the 2mm guide socket group were significantly higher than the other groups (p&lt;0.01). This study demonstrated that the 60 pcf polyurethane block can be used for in vitro cortical bone modelling and that the creation of a 2mm deep guide socket increased the primary stability of the 1.8 x 8mm mushroom head miniscrew.
